title.rendered: FIFA crisis deepens as Infantino meets senior staff over failed FFE plan

content.rendered:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is set to hold a crisis meeting with senior FIFA officials in Rabat, Morocco, on Wednesday as mounting pressure continues to build following the collapse of his controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

The emergency talks come after Infantino was forced to abandon plans to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise, a commercial subsidiary that would have overseen the commercial and operational rights of FIFA’s major tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup and Club World Cup.

Read Also: UEFA declares no confidence in Infantino’s FIFA leadership

FFE withdrawal deepens leadership crisis

The proposal, which included plans to sell a 20 percent stake in the new company to private investors, triggered fierce opposition from football stakeholders across the globe.

The project was first revealed in reports by The Times and the Financial Times before FIFA confirmed key details. The plan was formally withdrawn last weekend after facing widespread resistance from continental football bodies and national associations.

Read Also: European FAs demand new FIFA leadership, call for Gianni Infantino’s removal

The abandoned proposal has since plunged FIFA into one of its biggest governance crises in recent years, prompting calls for greater transparency and accountability within world football’s governing body.

Wenger distances himself from proposal

FIFA’s Chief of Global Football Development, Arsène Wenger, publicly distanced himself from the project, saying he had no involvement in its development.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Wenger said withdrawing the proposal was “absolutely necessary and beyond question.”

He also stressed his commitment to transparent governance, saying: “I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.”

Read Also: Infantino seeks Trump backing as FIFA leadership crisis deepens

Wenger had faced criticism in recent days for remaining silent over the proposed restructuring before eventually breaking his silence following the project’s withdrawal.

Top FIFA officials address staff

FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström also addressed employees in an internal email, describing the controversy surrounding the proposal as a “sad and reproachable series of events” that had now ended with the permanent abandonment of the project.

Grafström assured staff they would be protected from the political fallout, writing that employees would be “defended and safeguarded from the political context we currently experience.”

He added that while “individuals, unstable moments and unfortunate episodes come and go,” FIFA’s mission and responsibility to world football would remain unchanged.

His comments followed the resignation of Infantino’s senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, who stepped down last week after describing the FFE proposal as “a bad deal for football.”

title.rendered: Naira holds steady on improved FX liquidity

content.rendered:
The naira held steady in the official foreign exchange (FX) market on Tuesday, supported by improved market liquidity and stronger external reserves.

 

Data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed the naira appreciated by N2.28 as the dollar was quoted at N1,362.55 on Tuesday, compared with N1,364.83 recorded on the previous trading day at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM).

 

In the parallel market, also known as the black market, the local currency closed at N1,412 per dollar on Tuesday, representing a 0.21 percent gain from N1,415 recorded previously. The gap between the official and parallel market exchange rates widened slightly to 3.7 percent from 3.5 percent last week.

 

Total turnover at the interbank segment of the FX market increased by 13.99 percent to $156.23 million on Tuesday from $137.05 million recorded on Monday. The number of deals remained largely stable, rising marginally to 139 transactions from 138 recorded a day earlier.

 

Although NFEM turnover and deal figures for Tuesday were unavailable as of the time of filing this report, trading activity had strengthened significantly earlier in the week. The number of deals jumped by 50 percent to 333 on August 3, 2026, from 222 recorded on July 31, 2026, while total turnover surged by 130 percent to $532.25 million from $231.41 million over the same period.

 

Nigeria’s external reserves, which provide the CBN with the firepower to support the naira and meet external obligations, have continued to strengthen, rising to $51.94 billion as of August 3, 2026. This represents a 30.47 percent increase from $39.81 billion recorded on August 4, 2025, according to data published on the CBN’s website.

 

According to analysts at Quest Merchant Bank, Nigeria’s gross external reserves increased by $1.9 billion to $51.5 billion in June 2026 and were up by $2.3 billion on a quarter-on-quarter basis. The increase marked the second consecutive month of reserve accretion after temporary drawdowns in March and April, which were largely attributed to seasonal external debt-servicing obligations.

 

The analysts said the sustained recovery in external reserves has been driven by several factors. Despite a more uncertain global environment, foreign portfolio inflows have remained resilient, supported by Nigeria’s attractive carry trade opportunities arising from the CBN’s prolonged tight monetary policy stance.

Read also: Tinubu increases soldiers’ salaries from N100,000 to N250,000 from September 

They noted that elevated domestic yields, improved market liquidity, stronger external buffers and a more stable foreign exchange environment have further boosted investor confidence. The reserve position has also been supported by stronger export receipts, reflecting higher crude oil prices and a steady improvement in Nigeria’s crude oil production.

 

Quest Merchant Bank added that Nigeria’s external reserves are sufficient to cover 14.4 months of merchandise imports based on the balance of payments for the 12 months to December 2025, and 9.9 months when imported services are included.

title.rendered: ADC seeks fresh House of Reps vote over irregularities on state police

content.rendered:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC), has accused the House of Representatives of undermining the Constitution in its handling of the State Police Constitution Alteration Bill, alleging that the legislation was passed through a flawed process that lacked transparency, inclusiveness and due legislative procedure.

In a statement on Tuesday, Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, called on the House to recommit the Bill to a fresh constitutional process, citing reports that the required two-thirds majority was attained by recognising votes transmitted via WhatsApp from lawmakers absent from the chamber and by counting members who had signed the attendance register but were no longer present during voting.

“These allegations raise profound legal and constitutional concerns. The Constitution is not amended by convenience. It is amended through strict procedures that leave no room for improvisation,” he said.
The opposition party argued that regardless of the merits of establishing state police, constitutional amendment procedures must be followed to preserve the integrity of the legislative process.

Recall that the House of Representatives had passed the State Police Constitution Alteration Bill after voting on the proposed constitutional amendment as part of the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution.

The bill seeks to establish state police alongside the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen grassroots policing and improve security. Its passage, however, sparked controversy among some lawmakers and Nigerians.

The ADC said accounts by lawmakers who participated in the proceedings indicated that the constitutional threshold for the amendment was achieved through votes sent electronically and by recognising lawmakers who were not physically present when the question was put.

The party also expressed concern that meaningful clause-by-clause consideration of the Bill was curtailed and constitutional objections raised during deliberations were not adequately addressed.

“It is one thing to pass a Bill for political expediency. It is another thing to ensure that it actually solves the problem it was intended to solve,” the ADC said.

The opposition party maintained that while many Nigerians support the creation of state police to tackle worsening insecurity, the current proposal contains significant policy changes that have not been subjected to sufficient public scrutiny.

“The objective is not merely to establish another police institution. It is to reduce the insecurity that has devastated communities across the country. This new proposal demands careful scrutiny, not legislative manipulation,” he added.

The ADC warned that without rigorous public debate, the country risks enacting a constitutional amendment that reflects “only the echo chamber of the ruling party rather than the searching questions of the Nigerian people.”

The party further argued that Nigeria has repeatedly enacted major laws that later required amendments or reversals because they were insufficiently scrutinised before passage.

It therefore urged the House of Representatives to recommit the State Police Bill to “a constitutional, transparent and inclusive process” to ensure the eventual legislation commands broad public confidence and contains adequate safeguards against abuse.

AI governance failing to keep pace as global adoption surges, new index warns

content.rendered:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is spreading across the world faster than governments can regulate it and leaving significant gaps in public oversight, accountability and citizen protections, according to the 2026 Global Index on Responsible AI (GIRAI).

The report, released by the Global Center on AI Governance, found that while 128 of the 135 countries assessed have made some commitment to responsible AI governance, the average global score remains just 35 out of 100, revealing that policy implementation is lagging far behind the rapid deployment of AI systems.

The findings come as generative AI adoption reaches 53 percent of the global population and corporate investment in AI nearly triples from about $200 billion in 2023 to $581.7 billion in 2025.

AI systems are embedded in public services, education, healthcare, policing, finance and workplaces, the report noted.

Despite the proliferation of AI strategies and ethical frameworks, researchers found that evidence of implementation exists in only 55 percent of cases where responsible AI frameworks are active globally. The figure falls further to 45 percent across Global South countries.

“Responsible AI governance evolution has shown the limits of the framework-building phase,” the report said, arguing that governments must now shift from policy commitments to enforceable protections, transparent AI use and mechanisms that allow citizens to challenge AI-driven decisions.

The index noted that governments have been quicker to introduce AI literacy programmes than institutions capable of enforcing responsible AI.

Among 104 countries with active frameworks, researchers found that training courses and workshops were the most common implementation activities, while only 28 countries had independent oversight bodies, 22 had monitoring systems and just 16 had multistakeholder advisory processes.

One of the weakest areas identified was the use of AI in government itself as only 18 percent of countries require public disclosure of government algorithmic systems, while just 26 percent have frameworks governing the public procurement of AI technologies.

Researchers argued that governments are demanding transparency from technology companies without applying the same standards to their own AI deployments.

The report also found out that AI governance remains uneven across regions. Although Global South countries have significantly expanded responsible AI policies since the first edition of the index, most rely on voluntary or non-binding frameworks.

Framework coverage across Global South countries increased by 83 percent between editions, compared with a 35 percent increase in developed economies. However, 78 percent of responsible AI frameworks in the Global South remain non-binding, compared with 42 percent in the Global North.

The index further highlighted several governance blind spots. While AI literacy has become one of the strongest-performing indicators, labour rights, environmental protections, children’s rights and transparency in government AI use remain poorly addressed.

Only 39 countries have labour protection frameworks related to AI, while just 27 percent of countries have frameworks covering AI’s environmental impact.

The researchers also found credible evidence that governments in 35 of the 135 countries assessed have deployed AI systems posing unacceptable risks to human rights, including uses linked to surveillance, discrimination and other high-risk applications.

The report noted that the next phase of AI governance must prioritise enforceable regulation, stronger oversight institutions, transparency in public-sector AI, protection for workers and vulnerable groups, and greater cooperation among Global South countries to shape international AI standards rather than simply adopting rules developed elsewhere.

Resident doctors signal strike may be shelved after government deal

content.rendered:
Nigeria’s resident doctors on Tuesday indicated they could suspend plans for a nationwide strike scheduled to begin next week after the federal government committed to implementing key agreements within one week, although the association said a final decision rests with its National Executive Council.

Mohamed Suleiman, president of the Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors, dropped the hint after a meeting brokered by Femi Gbajabiamila, chief of staff to the President, at the presidential Villa, Abuja

The meeting had in attendance the leadership of the Association, Ministers of Labour, Health, and Finance, the Director-General of the Budget Office, the Accountant-General, representatives of IPPIS, Cash Management.

Suleiman, while fielding questions from state house journalists, after the meeting, expressed confidence in the office of the Chief of Staff to the President, adding that “I want to put it on record that this is not the first time the Chief of Staff has intervened in matters relating to resident doctors in this country.

“About six or seven years ago, when he was Speaker of the House of Representatives, he intervened, and each time he has gotten involved, our matters have been resolved. And today, I can tell you our matters have been resolved.

“Resolved in the sense that timelines have been agreed upon by various agencies of government.”

He also announced that the meeting agreed to commence the payment of salary arrears and promotion arrears.

“On the call duty allowance issue in LUTH, we have also agreed on a one-week timeline for implementation.

“We have also agreed on the number of house officers to be engaged. And we have agreed that house officers should not have to wait for a whole month before receiving the previous month’s salary. A standing order has been given that before the 10th of every month, salaries of house officers must be paid”

On the issue of promotion arrears, he revealed that “a one-week timeline has been agreed”

“On the Professional Allowance table, the government has made more concessions today on this matter”

The NARD President noted however, that there were still a few things that needed to be clarified.

“There is an outstanding amount which is not as high as we initially thought. Hopefully, the DG Budget will give us a timeline for when that will be paid. They have also extensively discussed mechanisms to raise these funds and pay us.”

Also speaking on the Collective Bargaining Agreement, CBA, Suleiman stated that the Chief of Staff has charged the Ministers of Labour and Health to fast-track its completion so that we will have the circulars and computations for budgetary purposes.

He added that “Whatever is agreed in the CBA will be captured in next year’s budget for implementation”

On the issues of harassment and assault of doctors, he stated that “31 doctors have been assaulted, and more than 20 other health workers have been assaulted in the last 10 months

He disclosed that the Chief of Staff to the President has taken it upon himself to initiate legislation in the National Assembly so that assault on health workers will be classified as an aggravated offense.

“We are very glad with that. We believe it will send the right signal that health workers should not be assaulted.

“Now, I cannot stand here and tell you that we have called off the strike. What I will say is that I have utmost confidence that what he has done today has moved the needle to a very large extent and has solved our matters.”

Middle Belt Forum backs Onaiyekan, says tackling poverty, insecurity critical to economic recovery

content.rendered:
Middle Belt Forum (MBF) has thrown its weight behind Cardinal Onaiyekan’s and the Catholic Bishop’s Conference of Nigeria (CBCN), warning that Nigeria’s worsening poverty and persistent insecurity are eroding economic productivity, undermining livelihoods and threatening national stability.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Spokesman, Luka Binniyat, the forum condemned what it described as unwarranted attacks on Cardinal Onaiyekan following his comments that President Bola Tinubu may not be receiving accurate information about the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians.

The statement followed the July 24 meeting between the CBCN and President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, during which the Catholic bishops reportedly expressed concern that the administration’s economic reforms had deepened poverty, increased hardship and failed to substantially improve security across the country. The President, however, maintained that his reforms were producing positive results.

The MBF said Cardinal Onaiyekan’s subsequent remarks on national television reflected the realities confronting millions of Nigerians and should not be interpreted as partisan political commentary.

According to the forum, the cleric spoke as a patriotic religious leader committed to justice, peace and the welfare of citizens rather than as a politician or opposition figure.

The organisation argued that communities across the Middle Belt continue to bear the brunt of insecurity, alleging that years of attacks by armed groups have left thousands dead, displaced millions of residents and destroyed farms, schools, churches and entire communities across Benue, Plateau, Southern Kaduna, Niger, Borno and other affected areas.

It said the humanitarian and economic consequences have been severe, with many farmers unable to cultivate their land, businesses disrupted, children forced out of school and displaced families relying on humanitarian assistance for survival.

While acknowledging the sacrifices of the Nigerian military and other security agencies, the MBF maintained that insecurity continues to prevent citizens from farming, travelling safely and engaging in legitimate economic activities.

The forum also questioned the real impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, arguing that although the national minimum wage had risen from N30,000 to N70,000, its purchasing power had been significantly weakened by inflation, exchange-rate depreciation and rising costs of fuel, transportation, food, electricity, healthcare and education.

According to the statement, the depreciation of the naira and sustained increases in the prices of essential goods and services have reduced the real value of workers’ incomes, leaving many households worse off despite higher nominal wages.

The MBF urged President Tinubu to embrace constructive criticism rather than allow supporters to attack individuals raising concerns about the country’s socio-economic conditions.

It called on the President to undertake an independent assessment of the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians, particularly victims of terrorism and violent attacks, saying direct engagement with displaced persons, farmers, market women, unemployed youths and community leaders would provide a clearer understanding of prevailing realities.

Reaffirming its support for the CBCN and Cardinal Onaiyekan, the forum said speaking out against poverty, insecurity and human suffering is a constitutional right, a moral obligation and a patriotic duty, urging government to treat such interventions as contributions toward national development rather than political opposition.

BEDC probes electrical incident as linesman injured during maintenance in Ekiti

content.rendered:
BEDC Electricity Plc has launched an investigation into an electrical incident that left one of its technical employees injured while carrying out maintenance operations on its distribution network in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State.

The incident, according to the electricity distribution company, occurred at about 6:20 p.m. on Saturday, August 1, 2026, around the Ado-Poly Satellite Campus area while work was being undertaken on the 11kV Basiri Feeder following scheduled maintenance.

In a statement issued in Benin City and signed by the company’s Head of Branding and Corporate Communications, Evelyn Gbiwen, BEDC identified the injured employee as Akinyemi Bamidele, a Technical Linesman, who sustained burns to his arm and other parts of his body after receiving an electric shock during the operation.

The company said the staff member was immediately taken to the Ekiti State University Teaching Hospital (EKSUTH), Ado-Ekiti, where he is receiving medical attention.

BEDC disclosed that Bamidele is in a stable condition and responding positively to treatment, adding that the company is providing the necessary medical and welfare support throughout his recovery.

The incident underscores the occupational hazards associated with electricity distribution operations, where technical personnel routinely work on high-voltage infrastructure under strict safety protocols to ensure reliable power supply.

BEDC said it has commenced an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident, noting that the outcome will guide any necessary corrective measures aimed at strengthening operational safety.

The company reaffirmed that the safety, health and wellbeing of its employees remain central to its operations, stressing that it will continue to uphold established safety standards while delivering electricity services across its franchise areas.

The Benin-headquartered distribution company serves customers across Edo, Delta, Ekiti and Ondo states, where it manages electricity distribution infrastructure and network operations.

NADF launches mechanisation training program to boost Nigeria’s food security drive

content.rendered:

The National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) has launched the National agricultural mechanisation service providers training programme, targeting 4,000 participants across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones to accelerate the country’s agricultural drive.

The 10-day initiative, implemented in partnership with AGCOMS (representatives of John Deere), the Industrial Training Fund (ITF), and the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (FMAFS), seeks to build a certified pool of tractor operators and mechanics to support nationwide food security goals.

At the launch held at the CSS Farms Training Complex in Gora, Nasarawa State, featuring an initial cohort of 250 trainees, Mohammed Ibrahim, Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of NADF, described the programme as a critical investment in human capital.

Ibrahim noted that despite Nigeria’s vast arable land, agricultural productivity remains hindered by low mechanisation rates, insufficient technical capacity, and poor access to modern technology.

“The effectiveness and sustainability of any mechanisation programme ultimately depend on the quality of the people responsible for operating, maintaining, managing, and commercialising the technologies,” said Ibrahim, who was represented by Ernest Ihedigbo, the Fund’s General Manager, Technical.

Ibrahim noted that Nigeria’s tractor density stands at about 0.3 horsepower per hectare, compared to India’s 2.6 horsepower per hectare, describing the gap as both a challenge and an opportunity.

He said the training programme would address the shortage of skilled mechanisation service providers while complementing the Federal Government’s ongoing efforts to expand access to tractors and other agricultural machinery.

“The effectiveness and sustainability of any mechanisation programme ultimately depend on the quality of the people responsible for operating, maintaining, managing and commercialising the technologies upon which it relies,” he said.

He added that participants were selected through organisations including the Tractor Owners and Operators Association of Nigeria (TOOAN), Tractor Owners and Hiring Facilities Association of Nigeria (TOHFAN), Women in Mechanized Agriculture (WIMA) and the Agricultural Development Projects (ADPs), with deliberate inclusion of women and youths.

Also speaking, Samuel Aende, NADF Head of Mechanisation, said the programme formed part of the Fund’s partnership with John Deere for the supply of 2,000 tractors, adding that the training would create a pool of skilled operators and mechanics to support the larger mechanisation programme.

He urged participants to take the opportunity seriously, describing it as an important investment for both the trainees and the country’s agricultural sector.

Representing the ITF, Fatima Baidu, Training Manager of the Model Skills Training Centre, said food security could no longer depend on manual labour alone but required modern technology operated by competent personnel.

She said trainees would receive practical instruction in precision field operations, preventive maintenance and safety protocols, enabling them to become certified professionals capable of driving agricultural productivity.

Alao speaking at the event, Sadiq Halilu, Chief Operating Officer of AGCOMS International Trading Company Limited, encouraged participants to actively engage in the training sessions by asking questions and sharing experiences to maximise learning outcomes.

In his welcome address, Maruf Olalekan. Director of the Federal Department of Agricultural Mechanisation, commended NADF for investing in both machinery and human capacity, stressing that sustainable agricultural transformation requires skilled operators and mechanics.

Olalekan said the Federal Government was implementing one of Africa’s most ambitious mechanisation programmes through the procurement of 2,000 tractors, more than 9,000 implements and spare parts under the Nigeria-Belarus partnership, alongside the Green Imperative Project with Brazil.

He called on development partners and private investors to take advantage of opportunities in mechanisation service centres, equipment leasing, maintenance hubs, precision agriculture and local manufacturing, describing mechanisation as essential to achieving Nigeria’s food sovereignty goals.

title.rendered: APC to Adeleke: Stop accusing Tinubu, embrace issue-based campaign

content.rendered:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has urged Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun State to stop accusing President Bola Tinubu and APC leaders of plotting to rig the August 15 governorship election and instead focus on an issue-based campaign.

Speaking with journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, Senator Ajibola Bashiru, the APC National Secretary, dismissed Adeleke’s allegations of political violence and electoral manipulation as “fear of imminent defeat.”

During a campaign rally in Osogbo, Adeleke reportedly likened the current political tension in Osun to the violence that trailed the disputed 1983 elections in the South-West, warning against any attempt to manipulate the August 15 governorship poll.

“President Tinubu, I’m passing this message to you. Osun will not accept any rigging. We will go out enmass and vote and defend our vote.

“Don’t let what happened in 1983 repeat in Osun. Accord party has endorsed you as our presidential candidate, why are we suffering? Oyetola needs to be called to order,” Adeleke said.

But reacting, Bashiru said, “How can a sitting governor be crying over rigging in an election that is still 11 days away, when in politics even 24 hours is enough to change the dynamics?”

Bashiru challenged the governor to defend his record in office rather than “casting aspersions” on Tinubu and APC leaders, arguing that voters should judge him on governance.

He claimed Osun’s infrastructure and social services had deteriorated under Adeleke’s administration, citing dilapidated roads and a shortage of about 30,000 teachers in public schools.

title.rendered: Delta sets sights on year-end power overhaul, marine economy boom

content.rendered:
​The Delta State Government has announced that it will establish the Delta State Electricity Regulatory Commission (DSERC) and the Rural Electrification Agency (DSREA) before the end of the year.

​This initiative forms part of ongoing efforts to reform the state power sector, expand electricity access, and attract private investment. Government officials, regulators, and private sector stakeholders discussed these strategies during a panel session at the Delta State Economic and Investment Summit 2026.

​Panelists disclosed that the government is collaborating with the Ministry of Energy and investors to operationalise both institutions before year-end. Furthermore, public consultations will precede the rollout of the state electricity framework, followed by an investor toolkit outlining regulatory requirements and opportunities.

​Leveraging the marine economy

​During the summit, Blue Economy discussant Ronke Kosoko urged the Delta State Government to prioritise the development of its inland waterways to drive investment, job creation, and long-term revenue.

​Kosoko stated that Delta possesses the natural assets to become Nigeria’s leading marine economy, provided there is deliberate execution rather than mere policy creation. She highlighted that the Federal Government has already established the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy and approved the National Marine and Blue Economy Policy (2025–2034), leaving states to leverage their comparative advantages.

​Delta’s extensive waterways present vast opportunities in fisheries, aquaculture, shipping, inland water transport, boat building, and logistics. Kosoko pointed to Lagos State as a model, noting that strategic investment in inland waterways has attracted hundreds of millions of euros while expanding transport businesses.

​Empowering fishing communities

​To enhance financing and support, Kosoko advocated for the enumeration of artisanal fisherfolk using the National Identification Number (NIN) and Bank Verification Number (BVN).

​Equipping traditional fishing communities with modern boats, cold-chain infrastructure, and efficient transport networks will boost productivity, reduce post-harvest losses, and increase incomes. She also called for better integration between agriculture and waterways to facilitate the efficient transport of agricultural produce across Nigeria and other African countries.

title.rendered: Police inspector, Air Force corporal killed in fresh Plateau ambush

content.rendered:
Gunmen reportedly ambushed a joint security patrol in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State in the early hours of Tuesday, killing a police inspector and an Air Force corporal and making away with their service weapons.

Several community sources who confirmed the killings to journalists said the attack occurred at about 5 a.m. after four security personnel drawn from two guard locations mounted a snap roadblock along the Ganawuri–Sabon Gida Road.

The sources explained that, “while the team was returning to their respective duty posts, two of the personnel failed to return, prompting troops to immediately launch a clearance operation.”

During the search, security forces recovered the bodies of the missing operatives.

“Security forces discovered the bodies of the security operatives, one inspector of the Nigeria Police Force and one lance corporal of the Nigerian Air Force. Their service weapons had been taken by the attackers,” the sources said.

Another community member, who spoke on condition of anonymity said the bodies of the slain personnel were evacuated from the scene, while their motorcycle was recovered.

According to her, preliminary findings indicate that the ambush occurred in a volatile corridor.

“Preliminary findings indicated that the ambush occurred near an area previously occupied by Fulani herders, who had fled with their cattle before reinforcements arrived. The attack site was also close to a native settlement,” she said.

She added that, in response, security agencies had scaled up operations in the area.

“Security forces have since commenced cordon-and-search operations around nearby communities, while clearance operations are ongoing to track down the fleeing suspects and recover the stolen weapons,” she said.

Alfred Alabo, the spokesman for the Plateau State Police Command could not be reached immediately, but top security sources at the command headquarters in Jos confirmed that investigations were ongoing.

content.rendered:
…Says Nigeria has assumed position of pacesetter in renewable energy capacity development across continent

President Bola Tinubu, Tuesday, inaugurated Africa’s first renewable energy college, the Barefoot Renewable Energy College, Osara, (BARECKS), and the Green Hydrogen Research and Demonstration Pilot Plant in Kogi State.

The President described the citadel of learning as a “world-class edifice”, completed to international standards.

He noted that while the difficulty confronting Nigeria, a country “abundantly endowed with sunlight, wind, biomass and water,” had been “converting its endowment into megawatts, and megawatts into jobs,” that difficulty will now be addressed by the college.

The President was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, at the commissioning of the college, at the Confluence University of Science and Technology, Osara, Kogi State, according to Stanley Nkwocha, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications, office of the Vice President.

According to him, ” the Nigerian leader had always maintained that a government is measured by the industries it plants and by the households those industries feed.”

The President observed that with the Barefoot Renewable Energy College and the Green Hydrogen Research and Demonstration Pilot Plant now open for studies, the question about whose hands should build and maintain Africa’s future has been answered.

” This is the first institution of its kind on the African continent, modelled on the celebrated vocational colleges of India that turned unlettered grandmothers into solar engineers.

“If that method could light the villages of Rajasthan, it can light the settlements of Kogi, Ondo and Cross River. Nigeria assumes, from today, the position of pacesetter in renewable energy capacity development across Africa.”

He also expressed satisfaction with the speed at which the project was completed, pointing out that while, as a nation, Nigerians have become used to foundation stones that outlast the men who laid them, the college kept its appointment with the people.

“Two years ago, we stood on this ground for the groundbreaking of this institution, with red earth underfoot and the ambition of a few determined Nigerians for company. Today, we stand before a world-class edifice, completed to international standards,” he added.

The college which was built as “a vocational and technical institution to close the widest gap in Africa’s energy transition”.

He described the shortage of competent technical manpower, as the greatest challenge, which the college is now expected to tackle.

“Our continent has never suffered a deficit of intention. We have suffered the scarcity of hands trained to execute them,” he added, saying the college will produce technicians, installers, operators and maintenance professionals with practical competence in renewable energy technologies.”

Graduates from the college will be exposed to internationally recognised certificates of proficiency qualifying them for employment, starting their own enterprise and competing anywhere in the world

“A certificate issued in Osara must one day command respect in Nairobi and in Frankfurt.”

He called on development partners, the private sector, international organisations and research institutions “to join hands with the college to expand research, innovation and technical training,” assuring that”Nigeria is prepared to host and lead such collaboration.

President Tinubu applauded the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, and the Director General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria, who he said carried the project from the drawing board to the commissioning ceremony through their persistence.

He also commended Kogi State Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, the government and people of Kogi State for providing the environment that made the project possible.

Earlier, Governor Ododo said the inauguration of the college was a clear indication that Nigeria is on the path to sustainable development through investment in human capital.

He noted that the college will strengthen the country’s energy sector through capacity building, while attracting investment and creating opportunities for communities.

The governor commended the federal government for tackling the nation’s power challenges through strategic investments in the knowledge economy, describing the initiative as one that justifies continued support for the Tinubu administration.

Kingsley Udeh, the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, in his remarks, described the project as a major investment in human development and job creation, stating that it reflects the Federal Government’s commitment to building a knowledge-driven economy.

Udeh maintained that Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy depends on developing a skilled workforce in strategic sectors such as renewable energy, urging the pioneer trainees to uphold high technical and ethical standards as well as serve as worthy ambassadors of the institution.

Mustapha Abdullahi , the Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria, described the institution as the first of its kind in Nigeria.

He said the facility is equipped with smart classrooms, battery energy laboratories, a mini-grid simulation centre, energy efficiency laboratories, and other modern training facilities.

He explained that the college will produce highly skilled professionals in renewable energy research and development in line with President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

Also, the Ohinoyi of Ebiraland, Ahmed Tijjani Anaje, said the project will provide young people with valuable technical skills, enabling them to contribute meaningfully to national development, even as he thanked the federal government for locating the institution in the state.

Why most real estate projects lose value before construction begins

content.rendered:
NONA Creation Studio has explained why most real estate projects lose value before construction begins, noting that across West Africa, billions of naira are committed to real estate development every year.

The company explained further that many projects begin losing value long before the first foundation is excavated, not because of poor construction, inferior materials, or inadequate funding, but because the most important decisions are often made too late.

“Too often, architecture is commissioned in isolation. Branding follows months later. Visualisation is treated as a marketing exercise rather than a design tool. Cost planning begins after major design decisions have already been made.

Construction teams inherit unresolved drawings, while marketing teams are left trying to create compelling narratives around developments that were never strategically positioned in the first place,” the company said.

The result is familiar across the industry, and they are expensive redesigns, avoidable variations during construction, delayed delivery, fragmented project teams, and developments that underperform both commercially and experientially.

The issue is not a shortage of talented consultants, but the absence of an integrated decision-making process.

That challenge is precisely why NONA Creation Studio was established. Rather than operating as a conventional architecture practice, visualisation studio or branding consultancy, NONA exists to integrate the disciplines that most influence the success of a development into one coordinated process, which includes architecture, interior design, visualisation, brand strategy, cost planning, construction thinking, market positioning and project communication.

These are often treated as separate services. “We believe they should function as one continuous conversation. At the heart of this philosophy is what we call Design Intelligence,” the company said.

Design Intelligence is the deliberate integration of architecture, commercial strategy, human experience, construction thinking and market perception into a single decision-making framework. It recognises that the quality of a development is determined not only by how well it is built, but by how intelligently it is conceived.

“For us, buildings are not the starting point; decisions are. Every successful project is simply the visible outcome of thousands of deliberate decisions made before construction begins.

“At NONA, this belief is captured in a simple philosophy: Nothing Accidental. We believe excellence is never the product of chance. Every exceptional development is the result of deliberate decisions made consistently over time— from the first conversation to the final detail.

Buildings do not become remarkable accidentally; they become remarkable because intention is embedded into every stage of their creation,” Collins Chukwuma, co-founder, architecture & design intelligence at NONA Creation Studio, said.

According to him, this philosophy is implemented through the N.O.N.A. Framework, a structured methodology that guides projects through four interconnected stages, including Navigate, where project vision, stakeholder objectives and opportunities are defined, and Organise, where research, commercial strategy and design intelligence establish a coherent direction.

Others are Nurture, where architecture, interiors, visualisation, branding and technical coordination evolve into buildable solutions, and Actualise, where construction, procurement and implementation transform strategy into reality.

The framework is governed by decision gates that ensure technical, financial and creative decisions are resolved before construction progresses. Rather than allowing uncertainty to migrate onto site, it seeks to eliminate uncertainty while ideas are still inexpensive to change.

“This philosophy is reflected in the complementary expertise of NONA’s founders,” said Chukwuma, who leads the architectural strategy of the practice, and ensures every project is grounded in clarity, functionality, environmental responsiveness and long-term performance.

Olutayo Osunsanya, co-founder, experiential design & visualization at NONA Creation Studio, leads the development of Perception Engineering, translating architectural intent into compelling visual experiences, market positioning and buyer confidence long before construction begins.

Together, the founders have developed an integrated practice spanning luxury residential, hospitality, commercial, mixed-use and institutional developments. By bringing architecture, Design Intelligence, visualisation and strategic thinking into one cohesive process, they have created a delivery model where architecture and perception reinforce one another. At NONA, buildings are never the product – they are the outcome of clarity, intention and deliberate decisions.

For developers, this means projects that are more coordinated, for investors, it means greater confidence before capital is committed; for institutions, it means environments that support operational excellence rather than merely accommodating it, while for homeowners, it means spaces that improve everyday life, instead of simply impressing at first glance.

As West Africa continues to urbanise, the conversation around real estate must move beyond aesthetics alone. The future of development belongs to organisations capable of integrating design excellence with commercial intelligence, construction discipline and human experience.

That is the ambition behind NONA. Not simply to design remarkable buildings, but to help create developments that are conceived more intelligently, delivered more deliberately and valued more highly because the right decisions were made before construction ever began.

title.rendered: Customs to begin annual recruitment as 573,000 applicants compete for 3,852 jobs

content.rendered:
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) is shortening its recruitment cycle from once every five years at minimum to an annual exercise after its latest recruitment cycle attracted 573,680 applications for just 3,852 positions.

Bashir Adeniyi, the comptroller-general of Customs, announced the new policy on Tuesday while releasing the final list of successful candidates for the 2024/2025 recruitment exercise. Applications were accepted for just seven days from December 27, 2024, to January 2, 2025.

The exercise itself, which took up to 17 months to complete, produced 1,275 successful candidates for the Superintendent Cadre, 367 for the Inspectorate Cadre and 2,210 for the Customs Assistant Cadre, Adeniyi said.

“The time was taken because the Service was determined that the right candidates should emerge. Every candidate on this list has passed through several distinct layers of scrutiny: application screening, computer-based examination, and verification of credentials against the national identity database. Where a record did not reconcile, we went back and checked it again,” the CG said.

With 573,680 applications received for 3,852 vacancies, the overall acceptance rate stood at 0.67 percent, equivalent to roughly one successful candidate for every 148 applicants.

Competition was particularly intense for the Inspectorate Cadre, where 128,604 applicants competed for 367 positions, about one slot for every 350 applicants. 

The Superintendent Cadre attracted 276,995 applications for 1,275 vacancies, or one position for every 217 applicants, while the Customs Assistant Cadre recorded 168,081 applications for 2,210 openings, translating to one successful candidate for every 76 applicants.

“Many of you met every requirement the Service set. There were simply not enough places. I encourage you to remain engaged with the Service, to keep your credentials current, and to apply again,” Adeniyi said.

He acknowledged the lengthy delay in concluding the exercise and apologised to applicants and their families, saying the process had taken considerably longer than initially planned. “The wait was real, and I do not diminish it,” he said.

According to the Customs boss, an unusually high number of retirements among senior officers, which placed pressure on the Service’s administrative capacity, also contributed to the delay.

Annual recruitment

“The Nigeria Customs Service is moving to an annual recruitment cycle. Recruitment will no longer be an occasional event undertaken every several years. It will be a standing, predictable, yearly process,” the Customs CG said.

He disclosed that the 2026 recruitment exercise will open later this year and is confident that future recruitment would be completed within a single calendar year, from advertisement to the release of the final list.

Since 2008, there have only been four national recruitment cycles into the Service, BusinessDay found, each spaced by at least five years.

“It allows us to plan our manpower against known retirements rather than in reaction to them. And it means that a young Nigerian who is unsuccessful this year knows precisely when the next opportunity arrives, rather than waiting in uncertainty for an announcement that may be years in coming,” Adeniyi said. 

The announcement comes as the Service implements modernisation initiatives, including technology-driven risk management, tariff reforms and trade facilitation programmes aimed at improving cargo clearance and boosting government revenue.

Adeniyi said the latest intake reflects the Service’s long-term workforce strategy, with a median age of 26 years and nearly three-quarters of successful candidates below the age of 30.

“These officers will carry the Service through the next three decades of its work,” he said, adding that younger recruits would be better positioned to adapt to increasingly digital customs operations.

​Aggregated by geopolitical zones, the North West holds 735 places with 702 in the North Central, “reflecting the seven states in each of those zones together with the Federal Capital Territory.” The North East, South South and South West each hold 630 places, being six states apiece, and the South East holds 525, being five.

“The variation between zones therefore arises solely from the number of states each contains. Not one place was allocated at the discretion of any officer of this Service. The Federal Character principle has been applied in full,” Adeniyi said.

Successful candidates will now proceed to physical and medical assessments before receiving final approval from the Nigeria Customs Service Board.

Reforms expose untapped potential in compulsory motor insurance market

content.rendered:
Nigeria’s compulsory third-party motor insurance market could be on the point of significant expansion as reforms introduced under the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA) 2025 expose a vast but underutilised market, constrained by poor claims awareness, weak service delivery and low consumer confidence.

A new industry report by Leenkaz Insurance Brokers Limited suggests that while NIIRA 2025 has strengthened insurers’ capital base, expanded policyholder protections and introduced statutory claims timelines, the industry’s next growth phase will depend less on regulation and more on converting millions of compulsory policyholders into active insurance users.

The report, titled: The Protection Paradox: Nigeria’s Motor Insurance Reality and the NIIRA 2025 Reform Agenda, was unveiled during a stakeholder webinar attended by insurers, brokers, regulators, actuaries and investment professionals. It examined responses from vehicle owners across 24 states and the Federal Capital Territory and found a disconnect between compulsory insurance compliance and actual consumer protection.

Its findings show that despite millions of Nigerians purchasing third-party motor insurance annually, the product remains largely misunderstood and significantly underutilised.

About 61.2 percent of respondents said their vehicles had been damaged by another driver. Yet only 21.6 percent of affected motorists received compensation through the at-fault driver’s third-party insurance policy, while 77 percent never benefited from the cover. The report describes this disconnect as Nigeria’s “protection paradox”, a situation where insurance exists but rarely delivers value to those it is designed to protect.

Consumer awareness remains one of the industry’s biggest obstacles. Only half of respondents knew that third-party insurance covers damage to another person’s property up to N3 million, while fewer than one in five had ever filed a claim under their own third-party policy. Even more concerning, 76 percent regarded the product as nothing more than a compulsory licensing requirement, and over half said their experience with motor insurance discouraged them from buying other insurance products. The findings point to a major growth opportunity for insurers.

Industry experts at the webinar argued that Nigeria’s motor insurance market is operating far below its potential because motorists rarely exercise the rights guaranteed under the law. They warned that the industry’s current premium structure remains sustainable only because claims frequency is unusually low.

According to the panel, as awareness improves and policyholders begin pursuing legitimate claims under NIIRA 2025, insurers will need stronger reserves, more sophisticated risk pricing and enhanced capital management to support increased claims obligations.

Rather than viewing increased claims as a threat, the report argues they should be seen as the foundation for rebuilding trust in insurance.

The panel identified two key reasons motorists fail to seek compensation. Many simply do not know they are entitled to claim against another driver’s insurer, while others abandon the process because claims handling is slow, cumbersome and lacking transparency.

To unlock the market’s full potential, the report recommends a fundamental shift in customer engagement. It urges insurers to simplify policy documents, digitise claims administration, provide customers with real-time claim status updates and communicate claims settlements more openly to rebuild confidence in the industry. It also advocates developing a national claims and loss database to enable risk-based pricing and discourage destructive price competition.

Although the ongoing recapitalisation exercise under NIIRA 2025 has strengthened insurers’ financial capacity, the panel stressed that stronger balance sheets alone will not increase insurance penetration.

“Capital addresses solvency. It does not, by itself, pay claims,” the report noted, arguing that customer experience, prompt claims settlement and operational efficiency—not capital alone—will determine whether compulsory motor insurance evolves into a trusted financial protection product.

The report expects Nigeria’s insurance industry to undergo significant transformation over the next 12 to 24 months as risk-based supervision, digitalisation and recapitalisation reshape underwriting practices, pricing discipline and customer service standards.

Among its recommendations, Leenkaz urged insurers to treat claims settlement as a growth strategy rather than a cost centre, regulators to strictly enforce statutory claims timelines and expand consumer education, brokers to strengthen policyholder advisory services, and industry bodies to accelerate digital transformation and professional capacity development.

The report concludes that NIIRA 2025 has provided the legal and financial architecture needed to transform Nigeria’s compulsory motor insurance market. The next challenge, it says, is ensuring that motorists can easily access the protections embedded in the law, a shift that could unlock one of the insurance industry’s biggest opportunities for expanding penetration, improving public trust and driving sustainable premium growth.

UNICEF backs Kaduna’s six-month maternity leave as economic boost for child nutrition, workforce productivity

content.rendered:
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has commended the Kaduna State Government’s six-month paid maternity leave policy and the introduction of breastfeeding-friendly workplaces, describing the measures as critical investments that will improve maternal and child nutrition, boost workforce productivity and reduce long-term healthcare costs.

The commendation came during a press briefing in Kaduna to mark the 2026 World Breastfeeding Week, where UNICEF said the state’s policies are creating an enabling environment for mothers to exclusively breastfeed, improve child survival and strengthen human capital development.

UNICEF Nutrition Specialist at the Kaduna Field Office, Chinwe Ezeife, said the organisation, in partnership with the Kaduna State Government and development partners, is leveraging this year’s celebration to reinforce the First 1,000 Days Initiative, which covers the period from conception until a child’s second birthday.

She described the initiative as a package of evidence-based interventions designed to improve children’s health, nutrition and cognitive development while consolidating gains already recorded in Kaduna State.

According to Ezeife, the state’s six-month paid maternity leave policy represents a major milestone in promoting exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months of life. She added that the launch of the First 1,000 Days Social and Behaviour Change Initiative for Nutrition would further encourage families, communities and employers to support breastfeeding mothers.

She also praised the Kaduna State Planning and Budget Commission for establishing a workplace crèche and deploying caregivers to support nursing mothers, noting that breastfeeding-friendly workplaces enable women to continue breastfeeding after returning to work.

Ezeife reiterated UNICEF’s recommendations that mothers should initiate breastfeeding within one hour after birth, practise exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months without water or other foods, and continue breastfeeding alongside appropriate complementary feeding until children are at least two years old.

She stressed that maternal nutrition before conception, during pregnancy and throughout the breastfeeding period is essential for healthy child development, adding that healthcare workers across Kaduna have received training on Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition to strengthen counselling and improve infant feeding practices.

Expressing optimism about the state’s progress, Ezeife said Kaduna is expected to improve on the breastfeeding indicators captured in the 2023/2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey. She disclosed that mothers who deliver between August 1 and 7 are being monitored to assess early initiation of breastfeeding as part of activities marking the 2026 World Breastfeeding Week.

Speaking at the briefing, Kaduna State Commissioner for Health, Dr Umma K. Ahmed, reaffirmed the government’s commitment to strengthening maternal, newborn and child nutrition through sustained investments in breastfeeding promotion and support services.

Ahmed said the 2026 World Breastfeeding Week theme, “Breastfeeding for a sustainable Start in Life: strengthen what works”, underscores breastfeeding as one of the most cost-effective interventions for improving child survival, reducing malnutrition and supporting healthy growth and development.

She said Kaduna State would continue implementing policies and programmes that expand access to quality maternal and child healthcare while creating supportive environments for breastfeeding mothers in homes, communities and workplaces.

content.rendered:
The Benue State Government has flagged off activities to mark the 2026 World Breastfeeding Week and launched the ‘First 1,000 Days Campaign’ aimed at tackling malnutrition among mothers and children across the state.

This is even as Paul Ogwuche, Commissioner for Health and Human Services, expressed concern over the high burden of malnutrition in the State, especially in the Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps where food insecurity, poor sanitation and limited livelihoods have worsened acute malnutrition.

The event, which was held at the Benue State University Teaching Hospital, BSUTH, Makurdi, was organised by the State Primary Health Care Board in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Human Services, UNICEF and other development partners.

The 2026 global theme is “Breastfeeding for a Sustainable Start in Life Strengthen What WORKS” and it focuses on the role of breastfeeding in child survival, optimal growth, immunity and sustainable development.

Breastfeeding remains one of the most effective, affordable and evidence-based interventions for reducing infant mortality and preventing malnutrition.

He described the launch of the First 1,000 Days Campaign as a major milestone, adding that the period from conception to a child’s second birthday is critical for physical growth, brain development, learning capacity and future productivity.

Ogwuche noted that proper maternal nutrition, early initiation of breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, and appropriate complementary feeding thereafter are key to achieving this.

I also want to express concern over the high burden of malnutrition in Benue, especially in Internally Displaced Persons IDP) camps where food insecurity, poor sanitation and limited livelihoods have worsened acute malnutrition”

The Commissioner reaffirmed the commitment of Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration to strengthening nutrition services in Primary Health Care facilities through the expansion of Community-Based Management of Acute Malnutrition, CMAM, promotion of Infant and Young Child Feeding, IYCF, practices, and improved access to life-saving nutrition commodities.

Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship backs 12 early-stage Nigerian startups advancing inclusive education through innovation, evidence

content.rendered:
Co-creation HUB, in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, has selected 12 startups for Cohort 4 of the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship in Nigeria.

Cohort 4 introduces twelve founders selected not only for the strength of their solutions, but for the depth of their understanding of the populations they are building for.

Focused on solutions for learners with disabilities, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and underserved or rural communities, increased participation and learning outcomes for young girls and women, and education and skills data systems that strengthen decision-making and system performance, the cohort reflects a deliberate commitment to backing founders who are addressing the barriers that prevent millions of learners from accessing quality education and ensuring that innovation is designed for those most often left behind.

The startups span across four thematic areas. In the area of Learners Living with Disabilities, TrainDTrainer Ltd, Talktu, DAWN AI STUDY, and Efiwe are developing solutions that improve accessibility, teacher capacity, and inclusive learning experiences.

Addressing barriers faced by learners in underserved, rural, and displacement-affected communities, Ileemore Technologies Limited, Skillup Africa, and Lena are expanding access to quality learning in low-resource environments. Heels and Tech, NursePadi, Skilladder AI, and Lalitah are focused on improving participation, skills development, and economic opportunities for girls and young women.

Strengthening education and workforce data systems, Ribara Analytica is building data-driven platforms that support better decision-making and improve pathways from learning to employment.

“Cohort 4 was designed around the belief that the most important decisions about inclusion are made at the earliest stages of innovation,” said Nissi Madu, Managing Partner at CcHUB.

“This cohort represents founders who are building with this understanding at the core of their solutions. These founders are tackling some of the most persistent barriers to equitable education through solutions designed with inclusion at their core. Our role is to help them test, refine, and generate evidence for their solutions while building sustainable businesses that can scale their impact.

Through this support, we are working to ensure no learner is left behind and that these solutions contribute to more inclusive education systems and Africa’s long-term prosperity.”

Each startup enters an 18-month programme that provides up to $100,000 in equity-free funding, structured technical assistance across product development, communications, and business strategy, access to CcHUB’s established ecosystem of sector relationships, and a dedicated pilot framework for building and documenting evidence of impact.

The Fellowship also equips founders with media readiness support and stakeholder engagement infrastructure, ensuring that the work they do over the next eighteen months is visible to the partners, funders, and communities it is most relevant to.

“At its best, EdTech does not just digitize education; it redistributes opportunity, and that’s where the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship comes in.

The Fellowship sits at the intersection of three powerful forces – education system transformation, inclusive technology-enabled solutions, and sustainability of Africa’s EdTech entrepreneurship,” said Wariko Waita, Director of the Centre for Innovative Teaching and Learning (CITL) at the Mastercard Foundation.

Since its launch, the Fellowship has supported 72 companies across Africa, reaching over 700,000 new learners, 89 percent of them children and youth, with a gender distribution of 49 percent female and 51 percent male.

title.rendered: WAFU B U20: Flying Eagles battle Ivory Coast for final, AFCON ticket

content.rendered:
Nigeria’s Flying Eagles will be aiming to secure a place in the final of the WAFU B U20 Championship and seal qualification for next year’s U20 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) when they face hosts Ivory Coast in Wednesday’s semi-final.

The high-stakes encounter will take place at the Stade Charles Konan Banny in Yamoussoukro, with the defending champions seeking to keep alive their hopes of retaining the regional title.

Flying Eagles seek response after Burkina Faso defeat
Nigeria advanced to the semi-finals as runners-up in Group B after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Burkina Faso’s Young Stallions in their final group-stage match.

Coach Abdu Maikaba’s side will be eager to bounce back from that setback against an Ivorian team that has been one of the standout performers of the tournament.

The hosts head into the last-four clash with a perfect record, having won all their group matches while scoring seven goals without conceding a single goal.

History favours Nigeria

The two teams last met in the decisive group-stage match of the 2024 WAFU B U20 Championship in Togo, where the Flying Eagles staged a comeback to defeat Côte d’Ivoire 2-1 in Lomé.

Goals from Clinton Jephta and Kparobo Arierhi overturned an early deficit and sent the seven-time African champions into the semi-finals, before they went on to lift the tournament trophy.

Nigeria will be hoping history repeats itself as they seek another famous victory over the Young Elephants.

AFCON ticket at stake

Maikaba is expected to make changes to his starting lineup following the disappointing defeat to Burkina Faso as he looks to inject fresh energy into the team.

Victory over Ivory Coast would book Nigeria’s place in Sunday’s final and guarantee qualification for the 2027 U20 AFCON alongside hosts Ghana.

A win would also move the Flying Eagles one step closer to successfully defending the WAFU B U20 title they won two years ago, reaffirming their status as one of the region’s dominant youth football teams.

title.rendered: Akwa Ibom First Lady flags off Ibom open maternity project

content.rendered:
Helen Eno Obareki, the Coordinator of the office of the First Lady of Akwa Ibom State, has urged nursing mothers to embrace exclusive breastfeeding, describing breast milk as the safest, most complete and cost-effective source of nutrition for infants, capable of giving every child a healthy start in life.

Obareki gave the charge on Saturday during the official flag-off of the Ibom Open Maternity (IOM) Project 2026, and the commencement of activities marking the 2026 World Breastfeeding Week in Akwa Ibom State.

Represented by Inibehe Silas Etukudo, the Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Welfare, she urged mothers not to deny their babies breast milk, stressing that breastfeeding remains one of the most effective and affordable ways of giving children a healthy start in life.

“God gave mothers breast milk freely, and it is sufficient for every child. No mother should deny her baby the benefit of breastfeeding because it provides the nourishment every child needs for healthy growth and development.” She said.

She described the Ibom Open Maternity Project as a life-changing initiative that demonstrates the commitment of Governor Umo Eno’s administration to improving maternal and child healthcare across Akwa Ibom State.

According to her, the advocacy walk from the Globe Roundabout through Aka Road to the ARISE Unity Park symbolised the collective resolve of government, development partners and stakeholders to champion maternal and child health across the state.

Obareki announced that the medical outreach component of the project is designed to deliver free healthcare services directly to women and children in rural communities.

She explained that the outreach was deliberately structured to reach the grassroots, ensuring that pregnant women, nursing mothers and children in remote communities benefit from quality healthcare without the burden of travelling long distances.

She therefore called on Local Government Chairmen and wives of the Chairmen, women groups, healthcare workers, Non-Governmental Organisations and community leaders in the benefiting Local Government Councils to intensify sensitisation efforts to ensure massive participation in the programme.

She encouraged women across the state to enrol in the Akwa Ibom State Health Insurance Scheme, describing it as one of Governor Umo Eno’s landmark healthcare initiatives aimed at providing affordable and accessible medical care for residents.

“This project is taking healthcare to the doorsteps of our people. We want every mother, especially those in our rural communities, to take advantage of these services and live healthier lives.” She said.

She commended development partners, medical personnel, women organisations, youths and other stakeholders for supporting the initiative, noting that their collaboration would further strengthen efforts to improve maternal and child health outcomes in Akwa Ibom State.

Eno Attah, the Executive Secretary, Akwa Ibom State Primary Healthcare Development Agency, encouraged mothers to exclusively breastfeed their babies for the first six months of life and to continue breastfeeding with appropriate complementary feeding until the child is two years old.

Attah emphasised that exclusive breastfeeding is essential for the healthy growth and development of infants, noting that breast milk provides complete nutrition for babies in their first six months, boosts their immunity, and reduces the risk of childhood illnesses.

In her remarks, Mary Udoh, the Chairman of the Medical Women Association of Nigeria, MWAN,, described the benefits of breastfeeding as immeasurable, noting that it promotes healthy child development, while fostering a strong emotional connection between mother and child.

Dr Udoh commended the various partners and stakeholders for supporting the breastfeeding campaign and for helping to spread awareness across communities in the state, calling on mothers to embrace recommended breastfeeding practices to ensure healthier outcomes for both mothers and their children.

Representatives of the World Health Organisation (WHO, Ibom Air, Nigeria Association of Women Journalists (NAWOJ, the National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS, Excellence Community Education Welfare Scheme, ECEWS and other partners reaffirmed their support for the advocacy.

They stressed the need to sustain breastfeeding practices, describing them as critical to improving child survival, strengthening the bond between mothers and their babies, and promoting the overall health and well-being of families.

title.rendered: 1,000 traders receive customised tables from Akwa Ibom business community      ANIEFIOK UDONQUAK, Uyo  ​  1000 traders have received customised tables from Akwa Ibom business community as part of efforts to boost small businesses in the state.      Helen Obareki, Governor Umo Eno’s daughter who kick-started the distribution of the 1,000 customised tables and umbrellas to traders across the state.      ​The empowerment initiative, fully sponsored by the Akwa Ibom State Business Community, marks a significant scale-up of the marketplace interventions originally championed by Patience Umo Eno, who had launched branded aprons for market women in 2024 before her passing     ​Speaking at the event, Obareki who also the coordinator of the first lady reflected on her mother’s deep empathy for the retail driving force of the state.  ​”Today’s event is incredibly special, not just because of the items to be distributed, but because it represents the fulfillment of a sacred vision.      “This noble initiative was first endorsed in 2024 by my beloved mother, Patience Umo Eno. She carried the welfare of market women close to her heart, and today, we are here to ensure that her beautiful legacy of love, care, and grassroots economic empowerment lives on vividly,” she stated.      She launched the distribution of aprons to give identity, structure, and a sense of pride to our mothers and sisters in the marketplace,” Obareki recalled.   Obareki, who was represented by Glory Edet, a former member of the state executive council described market women as the “economic engines” and heartbeat of Akwa Ibom communities, acknowledging their invaluable contributions to the state’s economy. Tinubu flags off N178bn Kaduna-Birnin Gwari highway, boosting trade, investment prospects

content.rendered:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday flagged off the construction of the 122-kilometre Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road, a N178.12 billion federal infrastructure project expected to strengthen trade, reduce transport costs, restore economic activities and deepen investment across one of Kaduna State’s strategic agricultural and commercial corridors.

The project, which already has more than N100 billion released to accelerate execution, is expected to reconnect Birnin Gwari to major markets after years of insecurity disrupted farming, commerce and the movement of goods and people. The highway links Mando in Kaduna to Birnin Gwari town and forms a critical segment of the wider Kaduna–Lagos transport corridor, providing a direct route to Nigeria’s commercial capital.

Representing President Tinubu at the groundbreaking ceremony in Afaka, the Minister of Works, Senator Engr. David Nweze Umahi, said the project underscores the Federal Government’s commitment to rebuilding strategic infrastructure that will stimulate economic growth, improve national connectivity and support long-term development.

The road will be constructed using Continuously Reinforced Concrete Pavement (CRCP) technology, a rigid pavement system designed to provide durability with a lifespan estimated at up to 100 years, significantly reducing future maintenance costs while improving transport efficiency.

The ceremony attracted top government officials, including Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, Deputy Governor Hadiza Sabuwa Balarabe, Minister of State for Works Bello M. Goronyo, Minister of Environment Balarabe Abbas Lawal, Minister of Housing and Urban Development Muttaqha Rabe Darma, Special Adviser to the President on Political and Other Matters Ibrahim Masari, former Kaduna State Governor Ramalan Yero and other dignitaries.

Governor Uba Sani described the commencement of the project as a major milestone in the administration’s efforts to unlock the economic potential of Birnin Gwari and neighbouring communities, noting that improved security has created the enabling environment for such large-scale investments.

He recalled that the Federal Government recently approved N178.12 billion for the highway project and released over ₦100 billion to ensure immediate mobilisation to site.

According to the governor, Birnin Gwari, once regarded as one of the country’s most insecure locations, is witnessing gradual restoration of normal life through sustained security operations and collaboration between the state and federal governments.

He noted that markets that had remained shut for more than a decade are reopening, abandoned farmlands have returned to cultivation, while construction is ongoing on the 36-kilometre Bagoma–Gagumi Road to improve rural connectivity.

The governor said the groundbreaking ceremony demonstrates the strong partnership between the Federal Government and Kaduna State in addressing infrastructure deficits while consolidating security gains, adding that improved roads will encourage agricultural production, facilitate commerce and improve access to social services.

The Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road has long been regarded as one of Nigeria’s most critical yet neglected highways, with years of poor condition and insecurity limiting economic activities along the route. Its reconstruction is expected to enhance regional integration, improve logistics for businesses and strengthen Kaduna’s position as a key gateway linking Northern and Southern Nigeria.
